plotSections.title: Potions of vitality at Qualin's Quax
bullets: Quaylin shows Walker four potions of vitality in a five-vial crate; each removes all exhaustion from a long adventuring day, cures poison and similar ailments, and improves the next short rest.
The fuchsia potions cost twelve hundred gold apiece and come with the Quax guarantee.
Walker is too exhausted to haggle and cannot afford them.
Quaylin tells Walker he can borrow liquid gold directly from the Haven Hold dragon at low interest without running another Sunder Chase.
Walker reluctantly decides to go speak with the dragon.

plotSections.title: Walker's gold hand
bullets: Quaylin taps Walker's gold-colored hand with a pestle and confirms it is real flesh, not metal for sale.
Walker says the change happened while swimming underwater in cold molten-looking water, possibly near the Temple of I in the north.
He put only his hand into the substance and it turned gold; he did not test anything else because he was underwater and panicked.
Plymouth signals Walker to stop discussing the incident in the shop.
Quaylin and Walker share a mutual dislike of loon folk.

plotSections.title: Leaving the apothecary
bullets: Plymouth confirms he secured several pounds of dragon gizzard from Quaylin.
Walker leaves Qualin's Quax and heads to the Haven Hold dragon to seek funds for exhaustion relief.
Quaylin says Walker may come back later when the potions might be on sale.

plotSections.title: Main party on the boat
bullets: While Walker shops in Sunder, the rest of the party remains invisible on the boat and still cannot hear one another.
Gerk remains confused and largely unable to act.
Ord’s olive-oil dragon-vessel outline is still faintly visible but has mostly dissipated over time.

The DM notes the party could theoretically exploit cross-realm economics across six of Atlas’s eight Arch realms, using keystone access and foreknowledge of door openings to day-trade or cause economic hardship against the lich.

newTerms.name: Loon folk
notes: Aquatic people Quaylin despises.
Said to be biologically inferior, unable to walk on land, and prone to trapping themselves in shallow puddles.

newTerms.name: Quax guarantee
notes: Qualin's Quax refund policy: if a purchased item quacks or cracks, the buyer gets their money back.

newTerms.name: Cross-realm trade manipulation
notes: With access to six of eight Arch realms, the party could theoretically build a cross-realm market and exploit door-opening timing against the lich.
